name: Green leafhopper (berdeng ngusong kabayo)
signs: Small bright-green insects that jump or fly off when the plants are shaken
Stunted plants with yellow to orange leaves and fewer tillers; this can be tungro, a virus the leafhopper carries
Yellow-orange leaves can look like lack of fertilizer, so look for the leafhoppers too
actions: Plant at the same time as your neighbors and leave a gap between crops, so there is nothing for the leafhoppers and tungro to live on
Transplant older seedlings, about three weeks old or more
Pull out and bury plants with tungro signs early, while only a few show them
Weed the field and the banks, and destroy stubble and volunteer rice after harvest
Ask the agriculturist for tungro-resistant varieties that suit your area
callExpertIf: Many plants are stunted and yellow-orange, or the signs are spreading across the field

insect.stageNote: from seedling to panicle initiation (when the grain head starts to form)
biological: Small wasps that attack the eggs
Mirid bugs and other predatory bugs
